It is also the correct reasoning, so not a defect, but the key is shortcut-reachable.

SM20A-B4.free_elimination: -21/4: graph is >= 0 everywhere and y = x - 21/4 is negative for x < 5.25, so the line can only meet the right branch - cannot make three points. Cheap sign argument. 1 and 4 need real work.
SM20A-B4.note: Key verified analytically and numerically (b=13/4: 3 points; 1<b<13/4: 4; b=4: 2). Explanation contains a false sentence: 'A line of slope 1 meets the two outer branches once each for every b > -3' - for -3 < b < 1 the line is below the left branch at x=-1 and never meets it (b=1 is exactly the threshold). Conclusion unaffected; fix the sentence (should be b > 1, with b = 1 the corner case). Desmos slider makes it findable but the corner-vs-tangent decision is genuine.
